Slice: Add Tool

Intent

Put a tool into the shed so neighbors can borrow it. The shed manager records the tool's name, an optional description, and its default checkout period. That period is the longest period a checkout of the tool can start with. A tool can be borrowed as soon as it is added: the Tool Catalog lists it as available (INV-TCAT-1), and Check Out Tool lends it.

Trigger & Actor

The shed manager, from the Tool Inventory screen, when a new physical item joins the shed. Each physical item is added on its own, including an item identical to one already in the shed.

Command / Input

Command: Add Tool

Field Type Required Rules / Validation
toolId ToolId yes A UUID chosen by the caller for the new tool, so a retried request is recognised. Must not belong to a different tool already added (INV-ADD-10).
name Text yes Leading and trailing whitespace (any Unicode whitespace) removed. Must not then be empty (INV-ADD-4). Need not be unique (INV-ADD-8).
description Text no Optional. Leading and trailing whitespace removed. Empty after that means none.
defaultCheckoutPeriodDays Int yes Whole days, 1 to 30 inclusive (INV-ADD-3). A fractional value is refused, never rounded.

Trigger

Triggered by: screen Tool Inventory @Shed Manager

Event(s) Emitted

Event: Tool Added → context Tools Read by: Tool Inventory and Tool Catalog (their own slices, right after this one); and, for the tool's name only, My Loans, My Holds, Overdue Loans To Notify, Undelivered Notices, Pickup Notices To Send and Flagged Neighbors.

Field Type Immutable Fact? Source / Notes
toolId ToolId yes From the command. Identifies the tool everywhere from here on.
name Text yes From the command, trimmed.
description Text yes Optional: absent when the command had none, or only whitespace. Otherwise from the command, trimmed.
defaultCheckoutPeriodDays Int yes From the command: whole days, 1 to 30.
addedAt Instant yes The UTC moment the event is recorded, set by the system.

Every field is fixed for good. No command changes a tool's name, description or default period; to correct a mistake, the shed manager retires the tool and adds it again.

Read Model / View

This slice produces no view of its own. Tool Added starts the new tool's entry in two views, each specified in its own doc:

  • Tool Inventory (slices/tool-inventory.md) lists the new tool for the shed manager.
  • Tool Catalog (slices/tool-catalog.md) lists it to neighbors as available to borrow.

Both are eventually consistent: the new tool appears once each view has caught up with Tool Added.

Invariants / Business Rules

  • INV-ADD-1: Only the shed manager can add a tool.
    • Neighbors do not add tools. How the shed manager is recognised is an open question below.
  • INV-ADD-2: Every tool is added with a default checkout period.
    • A checkout of this tool may start with a shorter period, never a longer one. An extension can later take a loan past it.
  • INV-ADD-3: A tool's default checkout period is a whole number of days, from 1 to 30.
  • INV-ADD-4: Every tool has a name. A description is optional.
    • A name that is empty, or only whitespace, is no name. A description that is empty, or only whitespace, is recorded as none.
  • INV-ADD-5: Each physical item is added as its own tool.
    • Two identical drills are two tools, each added separately. There is no quantity on a tool.
  • INV-ADD-8: Tool names need not be unique.
    • Two identical drills may both be named "Cordless drill". Each tool is told apart by its tool ID, not its name.
  • INV-ADD-9: Each tool gets its own tool ID when it is added, and keeps it for good.
    • The tool ID is how every later event, view and command refers to the tool. Names are only for people to read.
  • INV-ADD-10: Adding a tool with a tool ID that is already used adds nothing new.
    • A repeat with the same details, compared after trimming, succeeds and records nothing new, whatever has happened to the tool since. A repeat with different details is refused (tool-id-in-use).

Scenarios (Given / When / Then)

  • Happy path
    • Given: the shed has no tools
    • When: the shed manager adds tool T1 named "Cordless drill", described as "18V, two batteries", with a default checkout period of 7 days, from the Tool Inventory screen
    • Then: Tool Added is recorded for T1 with that name, description and 7-day default checkout period, and the time it was added.
  • Tool added without a description (INV-ADD-4)
    • Given: the shed has no tools
    • When: the shed manager adds a tool named "Ladder" with a default checkout period of 3 days and no description
    • Then: Tool Added is recorded with that name, no description, and the 3-day period.
  • Blank description is no description (INV-ADD-4)
    • Given: the shed has no tools
    • When: the shed manager adds a tool named "Ladder" with a 3-day period and a description of only whitespace
    • Then: Tool Added is recorded with no description.
  • Whitespace around the name is removed (INV-ADD-4)
    • Given: the shed has no tools
    • When: the shed manager adds a tool named " Ladder " with a 3-day period
    • Then: Tool Added is recorded with the name "Ladder".
  • A second identical item (INV-ADD-5, INV-ADD-8, INV-ADD-9)
    • Given: the shed holds tool T1 named "Cordless drill"
    • When: the shed manager adds a second, identical drill as tool T2, also named "Cordless drill"
    • Then: Tool Added is recorded for T2, a separate tool with its own tool ID. The shed now has two tools named "Cordless drill", T1 and T2.
  • Shortest allowed period (INV-ADD-3)
    • Given: the shed has no tools
    • When: the shed manager adds a tool named "Stud finder" with a default checkout period of 1 day
    • Then: Tool Added is recorded with the 1-day period.
  • Longest allowed period (INV-ADD-3)
    • Given: the shed has no tools
    • When: the shed manager adds a tool named "Tile saw" with a default checkout period of 30 days
    • Then: Tool Added is recorded with the 30-day period.
  • Period over the maximum (INV-ADD-3)
    • Given: the shed has no tools
    • When: the shed manager tries to add a tool named "Tile saw" with a default checkout period of 31 days
    • Then: refused with period-out-of-range: "The default checkout period must be a whole number of days from 1 to 30." No event is recorded.
  • Period of zero (INV-ADD-3)
    • Given: the shed has no tools
    • When: the shed manager tries to add a tool with a default checkout period of 0 days
    • Then: refused with period-out-of-range: "The default checkout period must be a whole number of days from 1 to 30." No event is recorded.
  • Period that isn't a whole number of days (INV-ADD-3)
    • Given: the shed has no tools
    • When: the shed manager tries to add a tool with a default checkout period of 2.5 days
    • Then: refused with period-out-of-range: "The default checkout period must be a whole number of days from 1 to 30." No event is recorded.
  • No default period (INV-ADD-2)
    • Given: the shed has no tools
    • When: the shed manager tries to add a tool named "Ladder" with no default checkout period
    • Then: refused with period-missing: "A tool needs a default checkout period." No event is recorded.
  • No name (INV-ADD-4)
    • Given: the shed has no tools
    • When: the shed manager tries to add a tool whose name is empty, or only whitespace
    • Then: refused with name-missing: "A tool needs a name." No event is recorded.
  • Someone other than the shed manager tries to add a tool (INV-ADD-1)
    • Given: the request does not come from the shed manager
    • When: it asks to add a tool
    • Then: refused with not-shed-manager: "Only the shed manager can add tools." No event is recorded.
  • The same request arrives twice (INV-ADD-10)
    • Given: Tool Added was recorded for tool T1, "Cordless drill", 7 days
    • When: the same Add Tool request for T1, "Cordless drill", 7 days, arrives again
    • Then: the request succeeds and nothing new is recorded. The shed still has one tool T1.
  • The same request after the tool was retired (INV-ADD-10)
    • Given: Tool Added was recorded for tool T1, "Cordless drill", 7 days, and T1 has since been retired
    • When: the same Add Tool request for T1 arrives again
    • Then: the request succeeds and nothing new is recorded. T1 stays retired.
  • A repeat that differs only in whitespace (INV-ADD-10)
    • Given: Tool Added was recorded for tool T1, "Ladder", 3 days
    • When: an Add Tool request arrives for T1 named " Ladder ", 3 days
    • Then: the request succeeds and nothing new is recorded.
  • A tool ID reused for different details (INV-ADD-10)
    • Given: Tool Added was recorded for tool T1, "Cordless drill", 7 days
    • When: an Add Tool request arrives for T1 named "Ladder", 3 days
    • Then: refused with tool-id-in-use: "That tool ID is already used by another tool." No event is recorded.

Alternate & Error Flows

Every refusal records nothing and returns one reason: the stable name, and the sentence shown to the shed manager on the Tool Inventory screen. The name is the contract; the sentence is the required wording of the message.

Reason Sentence Rule
not-shed-manager Only the shed manager can add tools. INV-ADD-1
name-missing A tool needs a name. INV-ADD-4
period-missing A tool needs a default checkout period. INV-ADD-2
period-out-of-range The default checkout period must be a whole number of days from 1 to 30. INV-ADD-3
tool-id-in-use That tool ID is already used by another tool. INV-ADD-10

tool-id-in-use can only come from a faulty caller, not from the screen.

A missing or malformed tool ID (not a UUID) is bad input, rejected before any rule is checked. It is not a refusal and has no reason name.

Idempotency: a repeated request with the same tool ID and the same details, compared after trimming, succeeds and records nothing new, even if the tool has since been retired or lost. So a retry after a lost response never adds a second tool. Because identical items are legitimately added as separate tools (INV-ADD-5), a repeat is recognised by its tool ID only, never by matching names or details.

There are no retries, compensations or external calls in this slice.

Non-Functional Requirements

  • Security / authz: only the shed manager may add a tool (INV-ADD-1). How the shed manager is recognised is the identity question below.
  • PII & compliance: none. Tool Added holds only tool details, and doesn't record who added the tool.
  • Performance / SLA: none.

Dependencies & Read Models Affected

  • Upstream events this slice relies on: none. Add Tool is the first slice on the timeline. Refusing a reused tool ID needs only the earlier Tool Added events.
  • Downstream read models / slices affected: Tool Inventory and Tool Catalog (a new entry); My Loans, My Holds, Overdue Loans To Notify, Undelivered Notices, Pickup Notices To Send and Flagged Neighbors (the tool's name). Check Out Tool and Place Hold act on the tool by its tool ID, and Check Out Tool takes the tool's default checkout period from it.

Open Questions

  • How does the system know that the person adding a tool is the shed manager?
    • No event or slice records who the shed manager is or how they sign in. Every shed-manager action (add, retire and mark tools lost; suspend and reinstate) depends on the answer.
    • (a) The shed manager has a sign-in set up outside the model, with a shed-manager role. Nothing about it is recorded as an event. (b) The shed manager is a neighbor account given a shed-manager role, which needs an event and slice to grant it.
    • Recommendation: (a). There is one shed manager, and nothing on record asks to change who it is.
  • Are there length limits on a tool's name and description?
    • Recommendation: name up to 100 characters, description up to 500. A longer one is refused with the limit in the reason, never cut short.

Slice: Tool Inventory

Intent

Shows the shed manager every tool in the shed on the Tool Inventory screen, and which of them are out on loan, to whom, and until when. It is the shed manager's working screen for tools: they add and retire tools from it, and record a tool lost when it is out and never coming back.

Trigger & Actor

  • Actor: the shed manager, opening the Tool Inventory screen.
  • What it shows: one entry per tool currently in the shed or out on loan, built from the events listed under Read Model / View. Nothing on this screen records anything by itself; its actions issue commands owned by other slices:
    • Add Tool (Add Tool slice) — always offered.
    • Retire (Retire Tool slice) — offered on every listed tool that is not already retired (INV-TINV-7).
    • Mark lost (Record Tool Lost slice) — offered only on a tool that is out on loan (INV-TINV-6).

Read Model / View

  • View: Tool Inventory built from events: "Tool Added", "Neighbor Registered", "Tool Checked Out", "Loan Extended", "Tool Returned", "Tool Retired", "Tool Lost"
  • Consumed by: the Tool Inventory screen (Shed Manager)
  • Freshness / consistency expectation: eventual — an entry reflects an event shortly after it is recorded (seconds, not minutes). No action on this screen depends on it being instant, because each command checks its own rules when it runs.

One row per listed tool. ToolId, NeighborId and LoanId are UUIDs. A Date is a calendar date in the shed's local time zone; an Instant is a UTC instant set when the event was recorded. A field marked optional can be absent.

Field Type Source / Notes
toolId ToolId Tool Added.toolId.
name Text Tool Added.name. Never changes. Need not be unique.
description Text Optional: absent when the tool was added without one. Tool Added.description.
defaultCheckoutPeriodDays Int Tool Added.defaultCheckoutPeriodDays (1–30).
addedAt Instant Tool Added.addedAt.
onLoan Bool Derived: yes from Tool Checked Out for this tool until Tool Returned or Tool Lost for that loan; no otherwise.
loanId LoanId Derived: Tool Checked Out.loanId while the tool is on loan; none once Tool Returned or Tool Lost for that loan lands. Optional: present only while on loan.
borrowerId NeighborId Derived: Tool Checked Out.neighborId while the tool is on loan; none otherwise. Optional: present only while on loan.
borrowerName Text Derived: Neighbor Registered.name for borrowerId while the tool is on loan; none otherwise. Optional: present only while on loan.
dueDate Date Derived: Tool Checked Out.dueDate, replaced by each Loan Extended.dueDate for that loan, while the tool is on loan; none otherwise. Optional: present only while on loan.
retired Bool Derived: yes once Tool Retired is recorded for this tool. A retired row exists only while the tool is still out on loan.
canRetire Bool Derived: yes while retired is no. Returned so the screen can offer Retire (INV-TINV-7).
canMarkLost Bool Derived: same as onLoan. Returned so the screen can offer Mark lost (INV-TINV-6).

Queries

  • List the tool inventory. Takes nothing. Returns every listed tool, each with all the fields above. There is no paging: the query always returns every listed tool. The order is an open question below.

Invariants / Business Rules

  • INV-TINV-1: Every added tool appears in the inventory exactly once.
    • One entry per Tool Added; nothing else creates an entry.
    • Each physical item is its own tool, so two identical drills are two entries.
  • INV-TINV-2: A retired tool drops off the inventory once it is back in the shed or recorded lost.
    • A tool retired while it is in the shed drops off at once.
    • A tool retired while it is out on loan stays listed, marked retired and out, until it is returned or recorded lost. Then it drops off. This lets the shed manager record it lost if it never comes back.
    • A tool recorded lost is retired by that, so it drops off too.
    • This differs from the Tool Catalog, where a tool retired while on loan drops off at once: neighbors can do nothing with it, while the shed manager may still need to record it lost.
  • INV-TINV-3: The inventory changes only when a tool is added, checked out, extended, returned, retired or recorded lost, or when a neighbor registers.
    • Neighbor Registered supplies the borrower names shown on tools that are out.
    • Holds and overdue notices leave it unchanged. Hold state is shown to neighbors on the Tool Catalog, not here.
    • A tool's details never change after it is added (see the note under Add Tool's event table). A mistake is corrected by retiring the tool and adding it again.
  • INV-TINV-4: Each entry shows the tool's name, its description when it has one, and its default checkout period.
  • INV-TINV-5: Each entry shows whether the tool is out on loan. A tool that is out also shows the borrower's name and the due date.
    • A tool is out from Tool Checked Out until Tool Returned or Tool Lost.
    • The due date moves with each extension.
    • When the tool comes back or is recorded lost, the borrower's name and due date are no longer shown on it.
  • INV-TINV-6: The inventory offers "mark lost" only on a tool that is out on loan.
    • Recording a tool lost ends its loan, retires the tool and ends its holds. It never counts as a late return for the borrower (Record Tool Lost, INV-LOST-3 to INV-LOST-6).
  • INV-TINV-7: The inventory offers "retire" on every listed tool that is not already retired.
    • A tool retired while out on loan stays listed but is not offered "retire" again.
  • INV-TINV-8: Applying the same event twice leaves the inventory as if it had been applied once.

Scenarios (Given / When / Then)

  • Tool added (INV-TINV-1, INV-TINV-4, INV-TINV-7)
    • Given: the shed has no tools
    • When: Tool Added is recorded for a cordless drill, described as "18V, two batteries", with a default checkout period of 7 days
    • Then: the Tool Inventory lists the cordless drill with its description and its 7-day default checkout period, in the shed, with "retire" offered and no "mark lost".
  • Tool added without a description (INV-TINV-4)
    • Given: the shed has no tools
    • When: Tool Added is recorded for a ladder with no description and a default checkout period of 3 days
    • Then: the Tool Inventory lists the ladder with its 3-day default checkout period and no description.
  • Two of the same tool (INV-TINV-1)
    • Given: the Tool Inventory lists one cordless drill
    • When: Tool Added is recorded for a second cordless drill, with its own tool ID
    • Then: the Tool Inventory lists both drills as separate entries.
  • Same event applied twice (INV-TINV-8)
    • Given: the Tool Inventory lists the cordless drill once
    • When: the same Tool Added for that drill is applied again
    • Then: the Tool Inventory still lists the drill once.
  • Neighbor registers (INV-TINV-3)
    • Given: the Tool Inventory lists the drill, in the shed
    • When: Neighbor Registered is recorded for Ana Ruiz
    • Then: no entry on the Tool Inventory changes.
  • Tool checked out (INV-TINV-5, INV-TINV-6)
    • Given: Neighbor Registered was recorded for Ana Ruiz, and the Tool Inventory lists the cordless drill, in the shed
    • When: Tool Checked Out is recorded for Ana borrowing the drill, due 12 October
    • Then: the Tool Inventory shows the drill as out on loan to Ana Ruiz, the name she registered with, due 12 October, and offers "mark lost" on it.
  • Loan extended (INV-TINV-5)
    • Given: the Tool Inventory shows the drill out on loan to Ana, due 12 October
    • When: Loan Extended is recorded for Ana's drill loan, with the due date 19 October
    • Then: the Tool Inventory shows the drill out on loan to Ana, due 19 October.
  • Tool returned (INV-TINV-5, INV-TINV-6)
    • Given: the Tool Inventory shows the drill out on loan to Ana, due 19 October
    • When: Tool Returned is recorded for Ana's drill loan
    • Then: the Tool Inventory shows the drill as in the shed, with no borrower, due date or "mark lost".
  • Tool retired (INV-TINV-2)
    • Given: the Tool Inventory lists a cordless drill and a ladder, both in the shed
    • When: Tool Retired is recorded for the cordless drill
    • Then: the cordless drill drops off the Tool Inventory, and the ladder is still listed.
  • Tool retired while out on loan (INV-TINV-2, INV-TINV-6, INV-TINV-7)
    • Given: the Tool Inventory shows the ladder out on loan to Ben, due 20 October
    • When: Tool Retired is recorded for the ladder
    • Then: the Tool Inventory still lists the ladder, marked retired and out on loan to Ben, due 20 October, with "mark lost" still offered and "retire" no longer offered.
  • Retired tool comes back (INV-TINV-2)
    • Given: the Tool Inventory shows the ladder marked retired and out on loan to Ben
    • When: Tool Returned is recorded for Ben's ladder loan
    • Then: the ladder drops off the Tool Inventory.
  • Retired tool recorded lost (INV-TINV-2)
    • Given: the Tool Inventory shows the ladder marked retired and out on loan to Ben
    • When: Tool Lost is recorded for Ben's ladder loan
    • Then: the ladder drops off the Tool Inventory.
  • Tool recorded lost (INV-TINV-2)
    • Given: the Tool Inventory shows the hedge trimmer out on loan to Ana
    • When: Tool Lost is recorded for Ana's hedge trimmer loan
    • Then: the hedge trimmer drops off the Tool Inventory.
  • Holds and notices don't change it (INV-TINV-3)
    • Given: the Tool Inventory shows the drill out on loan to Ana, due 12 October
    • When: Hold Placed is recorded for Ben on the drill, and later Overdue Notice Sent is recorded for Ana's drill loan
    • Then: the drill's entry is unchanged.
  • Listing the inventory
    • Given: the Tool Inventory lists the cordless drill (in the shed) and the ladder (out on loan to Ben, due 20 October)
    • When: the shed manager's screen lists the tool inventory
    • Then: both tools are returned with all their fields, with no paging.

Alternate & Error Flows

  • Repeated events: every event is applied idempotently (INV-TINV-8). A Tool Added, Tool Checked Out, Loan Extended, Tool Returned, Tool Retired or Tool Lost applied a second time leaves the entry as it was after the first.
  • Event for a tool that is no longer listed: under the rules above, a Loan Extended, Tool Returned or Tool Lost can reach this view for a tool that is no longer listed only as a replay of an event already applied. It changes nothing.
  • Stale actions: an action offered on the screen can be out of date by the time it is used (for example, "mark lost" on a tool that has just been returned). The command it issues checks its own rules and refuses with its own reason; this view raises no errors of its own.

Non-Functional Requirements

  • Security / authz: the Tool Inventory is the shed manager's screen; neighbors see tools on the Tool Catalog instead. How the system recognises the shed manager is the open identity question in Add Tool (slices/add-tool.md); this view follows its answer.
  • PII & compliance: shows a borrower's name while they have a tool out. It never shows their email. The name stops being shown on that tool once the loan ends.
  • Performance / SLA: none beyond the freshness above.

Dependencies & Read Models Affected

  • Upstream events this slice relies on, and the fields it reads from each:
    • Tool Added (Add Tool): toolId, name, description, defaultCheckoutPeriodDays, addedAt.
    • Neighbor Registered (Register Neighbor): neighborId, name.
    • Tool Checked Out (Check Out Tool): loanId, toolId, neighborId, dueDate.
    • Loan Extended (Extend Loan): loanId, dueDate.
    • Tool Returned (Return Tool): loanId.
    • Tool Retired (Retire Tool): toolId.
    • Tool Lost (Record Tool Lost): loanId.
    • All but Tool Added are specified in slices not yet written in depth. These names are this view's assumptions; each of those slices is checked against them when it is.
  • Downstream read models / slices affected: none. The screen it feeds issues Add Tool, Retire Tool and Record Tool Lost.

Open Questions

  • Should a tool that is out show when its loan is overdue?
    • The inventory already has the due date. Overdue would be worked out when the inventory is read, from dueDate and today's date in the shed's local time zone, so it needs no model change. It would be a bare derived field.
    • Recommendation: yes. It is what tells the shed manager a tool may be lost.
  • In what order are tools listed?
    • Recommendation: by name, with tools that share a name in the order they were added (addedAt).
